about: GRADER-BALANCE-1 golden fixtures for the owner's chemical-equation balancing ruling. ALL SYNTHETIC: CBSE-style questions (NCERT Class 10 Ch. 1 reactions) with typed answers composed for this lane, and the model reply each one is graded from (the step shape the stored golden replies show, plus the new optional equationFault / balancingEvidence fields). 'expected' is the result under the ruling; 'trunk' what d05e67a2 returned for the same reply. Driven on all nine surface rows by grading/balancing.surfaces.suite.cjs.
ruling: Owner ruling 5 Nov 2026 (GRADER-BALANCE-1, BAL-1): grade a little stricter than a CBSE examiner. An equation with the right species that is not balanced loses exactly 1/2, once per equation, never more for balancing alone. Type by what the student wrote: (1) wrong species or a formula/subscript changed to force a balance = conceptual (species mark follows the scheme); (2) coefficients written but wrong = calculation; (3) correct species left skeletal = presentation by default, conceptual only with a verbatim balancingEvidence quote of a failed balancing attempt elsewhere on the paper.

modelReply.teacherAnnotation: × H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide, not water: the product's formula was changed to make the atoms balance.

cases.question: (i) Balance the following equation: Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂ [1] (ii) Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction of zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid [2]
cases.studentWritten:
(i) Fe + 2H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 2H₂
(ii) Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂

modelReply.teacherAnnotation: × Fe and H do not balance; it should be 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.

cases.reading: (1) wrong formula (ZnCl) and unbalanced: conceptual, marks as the model gave (no cap) - the stored OA2-Q17 shape
cases.question: Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction of zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid.

modelReply.teacherAnnotation: × Zinc chloride formula is ZnCl₂ and the reaction is not balanced

cases.reading: 1/2 PER EQUATION: two skeletal equations in one step lose 1 (not 1/2 per step, not the whole step)
cases.question: Write balanced chemical equations for (a) the reaction of sodium with water and (b) the burning of methane in air.
cases.studentWritten:
Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂
CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O

modelReply.studentWork:
Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂
CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O
modelReply.teacherAnnotation: × Correct species, but neither equation is balanced.
